page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY core with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It operates on the x86_64 architecture with a base CPU clock speed of 2.5 GHz. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.mn4.large operates in lower performance tiers. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is rated as weak, falling into the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant drop from 158.75 GB/sec for cached small-block reads to 16.93 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Geekbench scores align with these findings, registering a single-core score of 939.0 and a multi-core score of 1598.0.

Due to its shared CPU allocation model and lack of local storage, the ecs.mn4.large is positioned as a budget-friendly option. It offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require sustained high CPU performance or high-speed local disk I/O. The primary tradeoff is the potential for resource contention on the shared host, which is reflected in the lower-tier benchmark results across database operations and text processing.

This instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, development and testing environments, low-traffic applications, and simple background tasks that can tolerate variable CPU performance and do not require high network throughput.
